why: Interfaces webref declares a constructor for that the BROWSER does not implement one for, and that neither the capture nor the IDL rules out on its own (SSOT W7.1, goal invariant I4: a generator's inputs are declared). `tools/sync/gen_shells.py`'s `_declares_ctor` settles every other such row from the capture (`ctor.length >= 1`, or `newable`) or from a required-argument-count contradiction between webref and the capture; this file is only for the residue where webref and the capture are CONSISTENT and both wrong, which the capture cannot detect because a shipped-but-throwing constructor and an absent one are the same two fields in it (`length: 0`, `newable: false`) -- `new CSSMathSum()` throws `Arguments can't be empty` and is a real constructor, `new AnimationTrigger()` throws `Illegal constructor` and is not. Only real Chrome separates them, so only real Chrome puts a name here. AN ENTRY GOES IN when `new X()` in headless Chrome answers `Failed to construct 'X': Illegal constructor` and a bare `X()` answers the unprefixed `Illegal constructor` -- the pair that means the interface declares no constructor at all. AN ENTRY COMES OUT when it stops doing that, i.e. when the browser catches up with the spec; a recapture is the moment to re-ask. Getting an entry wrong is one wrong message pair on one interface and `core/korvus-webapi/tests/installer_parity.rs` fails on it, because that gate asserts both shapes against the row for every interface of both realms. Measured in `google-chrome --headless=new` 150.0.7871.46 over a 127.0.0.1 loopback server, 2026-09-12, asking both `new X()` and `X()` of every own uppercase-initial global in a page and inside a real dedicated Worker.

interfaces.AnimationTrigger: webref's `web-animations-2.idl` declares `constructor(optional AnimationTriggerOptions options = {})` -- zero required arguments, so no count contradiction with the capture's `length: 0`. Chrome 150 ships the interface but not that constructor: `new AnimationTrigger()` and `new AnimationTrigger({})` both answer `Failed to construct 'AnimationTrigger': Illegal constructor`, and `AnimationTrigger()` answers the bare `Illegal constructor`. The spec and the browser also disagree about the MEMBERS -- webref declares `timeline`/`behavior`/`rangeStart`/`rangeEnd`/`exitRangeStart`/`exitRangeEnd` and the capture records `addAnimation`/`getAnimations`/`removeAnimation`, sharing none -- so the Level 2 draft describes an interface Chrome has not shipped, constructor included.
